issues.main_description_html:
Upgrade the Angular ESLint stack to the version line that matches Angular 21.

Scope rewritten 2026-07-30. The original body and its QA report were written against an Angular 13 / @angular-eslint@13.5.0 / .eslintrc.json checkout. The repository has since moved to Angular 21.2.9 with ESLint 9 flat config, so neither the old acceptance criteria nor the old QA findings describe this codebase any more. Original acceptance ("update @angular-eslint/* to ^19.0.0") is met — the packages are at 19.8.1 and ng lint runs. What remains is that 19.8.1 is three majors behind Angular 21.

Current state (verified 2026-07-30)

Package Installed Target
@angular/core / @angular/cli 21.2.9 / 21.2.7 unchanged
@angular-eslint/* (5 separate packages) 19.8.1 angular-eslint 21.4.0 (single package)
eslint 9.39.4 unchanged
typescript-eslint 8.x stay on ^8

ng lint runs and reports 673 problems (75 errors, 598 warnings). That is the baseline this issue must not make worse.

Why 21.4.0 and not 22.1.0

angular-eslint@22.x declares "@angular/cli": ">= 22.0.0 < 23.0.0". This project is on Angular CLI 21.2.7, so 21.4.0 is the correct target.

angular-eslint@21 peers typescript-eslint: ^8.0.0, so do not bump typescript-eslint to v10 even though v10 is published.

The current 19.8.1 install raises no peer warning because @angular-eslint/eslint-plugin only peers on @typescript-eslint/utils, eslint, and typescript. The Angular version mismatch is silent — nothing in the install output flags it.

What being three majors behind costs

11 lint rules shipped between 19.8.1 and 21.4.0 that this codebase would benefit from. Adopting them is tracked separately in #409.

Tasks

  • Remove the 5 individual packages: @angular-eslint/builder, @angular-eslint/eslint-plugin, @angular-eslint/eslint-plugin-template, @angular-eslint/schematics, @angular-eslint/template-parser
  • Add the unified angular-eslint@^21.4.0
  • Remove @typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin and @typescript-eslint/parser from devDependencies — both already arrive transitively via typescript-eslint
  • Rewrite eslint.config.mjs to extend the official presets angular.configs.tsRecommended and angular.configs.templateRecommended, instead of hand-spreading angular.configs['recommended'].rules
  • Confirm the angular.json lint target still resolves — @angular-eslint/builder:lint ships inside the unified package

Acceptance

  • pnpm install completes with no unmet peer dependency on @angular/cli
  • ng lint runs to completion
  • Problem count is no worse than 75 errors / 598 warnings

Follow-ups

This issue blocks:

  • #407 — Clean up stale ESLint flat-config for Angular 21
  • #408 — Enable Angular template accessibility lint rules
  • #409 — Adopt the 11 new Angular 21 lint rules
  • #410 — Resolve remaining lint errors and gate ng lint at exit 0

issues.display_title: Issue #407: Clean up stale ESLint flat-config for Angular 21
issues.main_description_html:
Clean up dead and incorrect configuration in eslint.config.mjs and the lint target in angular.json. All of it is stale relative to Angular 21 and typescript-eslint v8, and one item is a config bug that produces 42 false-positive errors.

Depends on #396 (the config rewrite lands there first).

Implemented in #412, stacked on #411.

Result

Before After
Total problems 673 641
Errors 75 41
Warnings 598 600
naming-convention errors 51 9

75 − 42 false positives + 8 newly covered = 41.

Tasks

1. Replace the removed createDefaultProgram option

eslint.config.mjs sets parserOptions.createDefaultProgram: true. That option was deprecated in typescript-eslint v6 and removed in v8, which this project is on. It is silently ignored today.

  • Remove createDefaultProgram: true
  • Replace project: ['tsconfig.json'] with projectService: true

2. Remove the prefer-standalone override

The config disables @angular-eslint/prefer-standalone with the comment "Project uses NgModule architecture (not standalone)". That comment is wrong:

  • grep -rl "@NgModule" src returns 0 files

  • src/main.ts bootstraps via bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, appConfig)

  • Components declare imports: [...] directly

  • Delete the '@angular-eslint/prefer-standalone': 'off' override and its comment

3. Fix the naming-convention filter regex

Of the 75 current lint errors, 51 are @typescript-eslint/naming-convention, and nearly all of them are kebab-case CSS design-token keys in object literals:

Object Literal Property name `bg-alternate-1` must match one of the following formats: camelCase, snake_case, UPPER_CASE
Object Literal Property name `text-3` must match one of the following formats: ...
Object Literal Property name `icon-color-2` must match one of the following formats: ...

The config already tries to allow these via its filter regex:

^(baseURL_GET|baseURL_go|CSGActions|[a-z]+(-[a-z]+)*|__.*__)$

The [a-z]+(-[a-z]+)* branch does not accept digits, so text-3 and bg-alternate-1 fall through and error. The identifiers are correct — they are CSS custom property names and must stay kebab-case. This is a config defect, not a code defect.

  • Widen the kebab-case branch to accept digits, or add an objectLiteralProperty selector with format: null
  • Verify the error count drops

Resolved — neither of the two options above was used. The regex already had one buggy escape hatch; widening it adds a second. format: null on a bare objectLiteralProperty selector would blanket-disable naming checks on every object property. Used the rule's own modifier instead:

{
  selector: ['objectLiteralProperty', 'typeProperty'],
  modifiers: ['requiresQuotes'],
  format: null,
},

Anything TypeScript forces you to quote is a wire format, not an identifier. Cleared 42 false positives, not the estimated 49.

4. Remove dead ignores, add real ones

  • ignores: ['projects/**/*'] — there is no projects/ directory in this repo. Dead.
  • Add dist and .angular so a bare npx eslint . does not walk build output. (Not hit today only because the builder passes explicit lintFilePatterns.)

5. Close the lint coverage gaps in angular.json

lintFilePatterns covers src/**/*.ts, src/**/*.html, api-modules/**/*.ts and misses:

  • server.ts
  • eslint.config.mjs — dropped deliberately

eslint.config.mjs is a .mjs file and tsconfig.json has no allowJs, so it is not in the TypeScript program. Adding it to the lint patterns while the **/*.ts block runs type-aware rules makes ESLint reject it with "file was not found by the project service". Covering it needs either projectService: { allowDefaultProject: ['eslint.config.mjs'] } or a dedicated non-type-aware config block — three-plus lines of config to lint one 120-line config file that the ESLint runtime already validates by executing it. Not worth the config surface.

server.ts was already in the tsconfig.json program, so type-aware linting works on it with no extra config.

6. Decide on max-len

'max-len': ['error', { code: 1000 }] is effectively the rule turned off.

  • Either set a real limit or delete the rule — do not leave it at 1000

Resolved — deleted. A real limit would mean a large reformat of the 6500-line main.service.ts, which belongs in its own issue if anyone wants it.

Acceptance

  • ng lint runs clean of all createDefaultProgram / dead-config warnings
  • @typescript-eslint/naming-convention error count drops from 51 to 9
  • ng build --configuration development still exits 0

The original acceptance criteria said "naming-convention <= 2" and "no more than ~26 errors total". Both estimates were wrong and have been corrected above:

  • naming-convention is 9, not 2. The estimate assumed only the two transferState parameter properties would survive. The real survivors are genuine findings: private methods missing their required leading underscore in elasticsearch.service.ts (2) and main.service.ts (1), an unquoted Authorization key at main.service.ts:6345, and 5 parameter properties across the two shared/translate/ loaders.
  • Total is 41, not ~26. The estimate did not account for server.ts entering lint coverage in task 5. It had never been linted and contributes 8 genuine errors — 4 require() imports and 4 unused Express handler args. New to the tracker, not regressions.

Both sets of remaining findings are #410's scope.

issues.display_title: Issue #408: Enable Angular template accessibility lint rules
issues.main_description_html:
Template linting ran with 3 rules. The 11 accessibility rules ship with @angular-eslint/eslint-plugin-template but were never enabled.

Depends on #396.

Implemented in #413, stacked on #412 → #411.

Result

Check Result
a11y rule violations found 2
a11y rule violations remaining 0
ng lint 641 problems (41 errors, 600 warnings) — unchanged, both findings fixed in the same PR
ng build --configuration development Exit 0

Original state

eslint.config.mjs spread only the recommended template config into the **/*.html block:

  • @angular-eslint/template/banana-in-box
  • @angular-eslint/template/eqeqeq
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-negated-async

The plugin also exposes an accessibility config that was not referenced anywhere. The Angular CLI's own generated ESLint config enables both. This gallery is a public-facing viewer, so a11y linting is not optional polish.

Rules this turned on

  • @angular-eslint/template/alt-text
  • @angular-eslint/template/click-events-have-key-events
  • @angular-eslint/template/elements-content
  • @angular-eslint/template/interactive-supports-focus
  • @angular-eslint/template/label-has-associated-control
  • @angular-eslint/template/mouse-events-have-key-events
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-autofocus
  • @angular-eslint/template/no-distracting-elements
  • @angular-eslint/template/role-has-required-aria
  • @angular-eslint/template/table-scope
  • @angular-eslint/template/valid-aria

Tasks

  • Add angular.configs.templateAccessibility to the **/*.html block in eslint.config.mjs
  • Run ng lint and record the new finding count
  • Fix the findings

Findings

Only 2, both empty anchors.

src/app/components/message/message.component.html:15 — <a href="javascript:;"></a>

No class, no handler, no content. Nothing in message.component.scss targets it. Dead markup, deleted.

src/app/villume-gallery/more-from-author/more-from-author.component.html:38 — .link-exhibition

.link-exhibition {
  position: absolute;
  top: 0; left: 0;
  width: 100%; height: 100%;
  z-index: 1;
}

A stretched overlay link covering the whole exhibition card, so it cannot carry visible text. Deleting it would break navigation. Given [attr.aria-label]="item.name" instead — the exhibition name is what a screen reader user needs, and elements-content accepts aria-label as an accessible name (confirmed in the rule source's safelist).

Note on the low finding count

The original issue predicted that interactive elements in the gallery viewer — artwork hotspots, navigation controls, dollhouse toggles — would be the bulk of click-events-have-key-events and interactive-supports-focus hits. That prediction was wrong. Both rules report zero, because every (click) handler in the codebase already sits on a <button>.

The low count is real, not a misconfiguration. Verified with:

npx eslint --print-config src/app/villume-gallery/villume-gallery.component.html

All 11 rules resolve to severity 2 on the largest template.

No rule was downgraded or disabled, so the acceptance criterion about documenting deliberate downgrades does not apply.

Follow-up worth raising separately

message.component.html:10 is an icon-only close link:

<a href="javascript:;" class="close-icon" (click)="showMessage=false"><i class="vi vi-x"></i></a>

No rule flags it — the <i> counts as content — but it has no accessible name, so a screen reader announces only "link". It also uses an anchor for what is a button action. Left alone here to keep #413 to what the rules actually report.

issues.display_title: Issue #409: Adopt the 11 new Angular 21 lint rules
issues.main_description_html:
angular-eslint 21.4.0 ships 11 rules that do not exist in 19.8.1. They cover Angular 21 idioms this codebase already uses — signals, @if/@for control flow, takeUntilDestroyed, host metadata.

Blocked by #396. Implemented in #414, stacked on #413 → #412 → #411.

Result

Check Result
Findings from the 11 new rules 26
Findings remaining 0
ng lint 641 problems (41 errors, 600 warnings) — back to the pre-change baseline
ng build --configuration development Exit 0

Rules added between 19.8.1 and 21.4.0

Verified by diffing the published rule sets of both versions.

TypeScript (@angular-eslint/*)

Rule What it catches Findings
computed-must-return computed() callback with a code path that returns nothing 0
no-developer-preview Use of Angular APIs marked developer preview 0
no-experimental Use of Angular APIs marked experimental 0
no-implicit-take-until-destroyed takeUntilDestroyed() relying on the implicit injection context 0
prefer-host-metadata-property @HostBinding / @HostListener decorators instead of the host metadata property 0
prefer-signal-model Paired input() + output() that should be a model() 0

Templates (@angular-eslint/template/*)

Rule What it catches Findings
no-empty-control-flow Empty @if / @for / @switch blocks 0
no-non-null-assertion ! non-null assertions in template expressions 0
prefer-at-else @else chains that should use @else if 15
prefer-built-in-pipes Hand-rolled pipes duplicating built-ins 0
prefer-class-binding [ngClass] where [class.x] binding is enough 11

Tasks

  • Confirm which of the 11 are already on via tsRecommended / templateRecommended in 21.4.0 and which need explicit opt-in
  • Enable the remaining ones explicitly in eslint.config.mjs
  • Run ng lint, record the finding count
  • Fix the findings

All 11 needed explicit opt-in. Confirmed with eslint --print-config against both a .ts and a .html file — none of the 11 is carried by tsRecommended, templateRecommended, or templateAccessibility.

How the 26 findings were fixed

prefer-at-else — 15, auto-fixed

Ran eslint --fix "src/**/*.html" rather than ng lint --fix, deliberately: the unscoped form would also strip the 4 auto-fixable unused eslint-disable directives in src/environments/, which belong to #410.

Every case was an exact negation pair, so the rewrite is semantics-preserving:

  @if (!fullscreen) {
    <i class="vi vi-fullscreen"></i>
  }
- @if (fullscreen) {
+ @else {
    <i class="vi vi-close-fullscreen"></i>
  }

prefer-class-binding — 11, fixed by hand

Not auto-fixable. Three shapes:

  • 8× [ngClass]="colorTone" → [class]="colorTone". colorTone is a plain string @Input in both splash-screen-preview and exhibition-unavailable.
  • 1× [ngClass]="'position-'+positionText" → [class]="'position-'+positionText".
  • 2× ternaries → paired [class.x] bindings:
- [ngClass]="mainService.openSideContent ? 'active-btn' : 'no-active'"
+ [class.active-btn]="mainService.openSideContent" [class.no-active]="!mainService.openSideContent"

Zero ngClass usages remain in the codebase.

Risk checked before merging

Six of the converted elements carry a static class and the new [class] binding — e.g. <div class="wrapper" [class]="colorTone">. If [class] replaced rather than merged, the static styling would silently vanish.

It merges. Confirmed in the compiled bundle rather than from memory:

consts: [[1, "wrap-exhibition-unavailable"], ...]   // marker 1 = Classes
ɵɵdomElementStart(0, "div", 0);                     // static class applied at creation
// update block:
ɵɵclassMap(ctx.colorTone);                          // binding merges on top

The static class is compiled into the element's const array and applied at creation; the binding compiles to a separate classMap call in the update block.

Acceptance

  • All 11 rules are active
  • ng lint reports 0 errors from them
  • Nothing deferred to warn — no follow-up issue needed

Note on the original relevance estimate

The issue predicted that the signals work from #401 and the inject() migration from #400 would make computed-must-return, prefer-signal-model, and no-implicit-take-until-destroyed fire. All three report zero. Every finding came from the two template rules instead.

issues.display_title: Issue #410: Resolve remaining lint errors and gate ng lint at exit 0
issues.main_description_html:
Bring ng lint to exit code 0 so it can gate pushes.

Depends on #396 and #407. Implemented in #415, stacked on #414 → #413 → #412 → #411.

Result

Check Before After
ng lint 641 problems, 41 errors, exit 1 594 problems, 0 errors, exit 0
tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit 1 error Exit 0
ng build --configuration development Exit 0 Exit 0

Tasks

  • Fix all remaining errors
  • Fix the parameter property naming errors
  • Remove the unused eslint-disable directives
  • Add a gate that fails on regression

Dead code removed

src/app/shared/translate/ — deleted, all three files. Nothing imported the @translate alias or either loader class, @ngx-translate was used only inside that folder, and the src/assets/i18n/ directory TranslateServerLoader reads does not exist. Also dropped @ngx-translate/core, @ngx-translate/http-loader, and the @translate path mapping in tsconfig.json. Cleared 5 errors, including the 5 parameter-property naming findings this issue listed.

this.executeUpstairsFunction = true in main.service.ts — inside a function event handler this is the canvas element, so this wrote a property onto the DOM node. A repo-wide grep finds exactly one occurrence: the write itself. Nothing ever reads it.

Real defects fixed

no-async-promise-executor — 3 sites

The issue flagged this as the one to treat as a real bug rather than a style nit. Correct: a rejection thrown after the first await inside a Promise executor is swallowed.

  • setupSceneEnvironment → plain async method. The try/catch that only forwarded to reject is gone; throwing propagates naturally.
  • _focusOnArtworkAnimation → async method. It genuinely needs a Promise, because it settles from an animation-completion callback — but that wrapper now holds only the callback, and its executor is synchronous.
  • unselectAnimation → had no await in its outer executor at all; the await lives inside a nested setTimeout(async () => ...). Dropping async from the outer executor was the whole fix, zero behaviour change.

no-this-alias — 2 sites

The four BabylonJS keyboard handlers (_onKeyDown / _onKeyUp on two input plugins) became arrow functions, so this is lexically the plugin instance and both const THIS = this aliases disappeared. Safe because the dead executeUpstairsFunction write above was the only place a handler relied on this meaning the DOM element.

Remaining

no-case-declarations, no-prototype-builtins (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call), four no-empty-function, nine unused args prefixed with _, and the four template eqeqeq sites.

require() → import

server.ts and api-modules/ used require() because those packages ship no type declarations — converting naively produced TS7016. The change therefore comes with @types/cookie-parser, @types/compression, @types/cors, @types/body-parser, @types/request. The Express middleware is now genuinely typed instead of implicitly any.

Naming

  • getClientIPData / getContinentName / _FogEffectFourWall renamed to match the project convention.
  • Authorization exempted through the config's existing filter regex rather than renamed — renaming an HTTP header name would break the request.

Test fix, not in the original scope

not-subs-dialog.component.spec.ts imported async from @angular/core/testing, removed back in Angular 12. Switched to waitForAsync. ng build does not compile spec files, so this had been broken silently and only surfaced once tsc --noEmit entered the gate.

The gate — local, per the team's decision

Not GitHub Actions. .githooks/pre-push runs ng lint, then tsc --noEmit. Wired via a prepare script that sets core.hooksPath on install — no husky, no new tooling dependency:

"prepare": "git rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1 && git config core.hooksPath .githooks || true"

The typecheck step is not redundant. The untyped request import passed ng lint with exit 0 and failed only at build time — exactly the class of breakage a lint-only gate waves through. That is why the gate is two steps, not one.

Verified three ways:

Scenario Expected Actual
Clean tree pass exit 0
Injected lint error (empty arrow function) reject exit 1
Injected type error (import * as request) — ng lint alone exits 0 reject exit 1

Bypass stays available: git push --no-verify. Cost: ~17s lint + ~9s typecheck.

Warnings — deliberately left

594 warnings remain: 588 no-explicit-any, 6 prefer-for-of. Left at warn on purpose. Typing 588 sites is its own piece of work, not a merge gate. Worth a separate issue if the team wants it.

Needs a manual look before merge

Two changes touch runtime behaviour in ways a build cannot confirm:

  1. The three animation refactors in main.service.ts — worth clicking through artwork focus, unselect, and room tour in the gallery.
  2. positionText == '3' → === '3' in the splash screen (4 sites). The interface declares text_placement: '1' | '2' | '3' | '4' | '5' and strictTemplates is on, so this is sound against the declared contract — but splashScreens is assigned raw API data, so if the backend ever sends a number the centering would silently stop applying. If that is a real possibility it is a backend contract bug worth surfacing, not something to paper over with ==.

issues.display_title: Issue #1747: [Editor] Artwork detail panel labels render dark on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Artwork detail panel of the editor (Artworks tab → select an artwork), several text elements render in a dark/near-black color on the dark panel background. Contrast is so low the labels are barely readable.

Affected text

Element Location
Frame slot name (e.g. df) frame slot row above the icon toolbar
Scaling scaling-image.component.html:3
Grid align section (app-align-object)
Bottom / Top align section (app-align-object)
Advanced Settings images.component.html:49
Artwork Info Button Artwork Info Button toggle row

Other labels in the same panel (Your Text:, Link:, Email:) render in a readable light gray, so the styling is inconsistent within the same panel.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Artworks tab
  3. Select an artwork to open its detail panel
  4. Look at the section labels listed above

Expected

All labels in the artwork detail panel use the same light foreground color as the rest of the editor sidebar and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark panel background.

Actual

The listed labels render dark on dark, effectively invisible without straining.

Notes

Shared editor styles live in _editor.scss (.content-slide .title-content, .content-input). The affected components (scaling-image, align-object) do not define their own text color, so they appear to be inheriting a dark default instead of the sidebar's $color-gray3.

Environment

  • Page: Editor → Artworks → artwork detail
  • Branch: development

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Publish tab
  3. Scroll through Cover Image → Add Links → Shareable link
  4. Look at the labels listed above

Expected

All labels in the Publish tab use the same light foreground color as the rest of the editor sidebar and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark panel background.

Actual

The listed labels render dark on dark, effectively invisible without straining.

Notes

Shared editor styles live in _editor.scss. Labels that define no text color inherit a dark default instead of the sidebar's $color-gray3. A single fix at that level should cover the Artworks, Objects, Text, Settings and Publish panels together (#1747, #1748, #1749, #1750).

Environment

  • Page: Editor → Publish
  • Branch: development

issues.display_title: Issue #1752: [Editor] Edit Frame dialog labels render low-contrast on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Edit Frame dialog (Artworks → artwork → Edit Frame), most control labels render in a low-contrast muted blue-gray on the dark dialog background instead of the readable light gray used elsewhere. The labels are hard to read across all four tabs (Canvas, Passepartout, Frame, Saved).

Same defect class as the editor panels reported in #1747, #1748, #1749, #1750 and #1751.

Affected text

All in edit-frame.component.html:

Tab Element Location
Canvas Thickness line 105
Canvas Color line 129
Passepartout Texture line 161
Passepartout Thickness line 218
Passepartout Width line 246
Passepartout Passepartout Measurements line 281
Passepartout Round Corners line 368
Passepartout Color line 401
Frame Thickness line 475
Frame Width line 503
Frame Frame Measurements line 538
Frame Round Corners line 625
Saved No data / Loading ... line 726

Readable by comparison: the dialog title Edit Frame, the tab names, Texture and Color in the Frame tab (rendered via <label> at line 425 and line 650), Save This Frame and Apply to all Artworks. So the same word (Texture, Color) is readable in one tab and low-contrast in another purely depending on whether it is marked up as <label> or <span>.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Artworks tab and select an artwork
  3. Open Edit Frame
  4. Walk through the Canvas / Passepartout / Frame / Saved tabs and look at the control labels

Expected

All labels in the dialog use the sidebar's light foreground color ($color-gray3 / #E7E7E7) and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark dialog background.

Actual

The labels listed above render in a muted low-contrast blue-gray, noticeably dimmer than the surrounding readable text.

Notes

edit-frame.component.scss styles <label> and button text explicitly but leaves the bare <span> labels without a color, so they fall back to an inherited value. Aligning the <span> labels with the existing <label> styling should fix the whole dialog in one change.

Environment

  • Page: Editor → Artworks → artwork → Edit Frame dialog
  • Branch: development

issues.display_title: Issue #1753: [Editor] Edit Splash Screen dialog labels render dark on dark background
issues.main_description_html:
Description

In the Edit Splash Screen dialog (Publish tab → Edit Splash Screen), the section labels render in a low-contrast dark color on the dark dialog background, matching the defect already reported for the editor panels (#1747, #1748, #1749, #1750, #1751) and the Edit Frame dialog (#1752).

Affected text

All in splash-screen.component.html:

Element Location
Overlay Tone line 150
Header line 165
Body line 195
Text Placement line 226
Button Text: line 253

Steps to reproduce

  1. Open the editor of any virtual gallery
  2. Go to the Publish tab
  3. Click Edit Splash Screen
  4. Look at the section labels listed above

Expected

All labels in the dialog use the light foreground color used elsewhere in the editor ($color-gray3 / #E7E7E7) and meet the WCAG AA contrast ratio (4.5:1) against the dark dialog background.

Actual

The listed labels render dark on dark, noticeably dimmer than the surrounding readable text.

Notes

Every one of these elements carries the .label class. splash-screen.component.scss declares .label four separate times — line 255, line 350, line 428, line 512 — and each one sets only font-size (and margin-right), never color. So the labels fall back to an inherited dark value while their neighbouring elements set $color-gray3 explicitly.

Fixing .label to carry the light foreground color covers the whole dialog in one change, and follows the same shared-fix approach as the sibling issues above.

Environment

  • Page: Editor → Publish → Edit Splash Screen dialog
  • Branch: development
